deviations: Review-blocker fix (old->new): the envelope's `precheck` is now a true canonical `entities.schema.json#/$defs/PeriodPrecheck` object — all required fields (id/organization_id/version/status/period/blocking_codes/last_event_ref/can_close), the full status enum, no warning_codes/non-canonical fields inside it, and additionalProperties=false — while checks/differences/issues/missing/summary/precheck_digest remain top-level envelope extensions. The contract adds a canonical field/status mapping table, requires schema validation by implementers/PH-353, and states that publishing extensions as a public query needs a canonical version bump. The report/docs no longer claim a partial/cropped canonical alignment.

The contract intentionally freezes a read-only projection (period.precheck.snapshot/v1) that extends canonical period.precheck.get/v1 with derived checks/differences/issues/missing; it explicitly states that publishing those fields as a public query requires a separate canonical version-bump planning slice, not this docs-only freeze.

The four reconciliation domains reuse existing owner read services and their issue_code vocabularies verbatim (cash bridge, settlement coverage, revenue pairing, bank charge pairing) instead of redefining rules; period precheck only aggregates and adds period/lock determination.
Cash offset (PH-241) and insights read models (PH-272) are not delivered; the contract represents them as offset_implemented=false/missing rather than treating them as zero or implemented.

precheck_digest binds a read-only precheck snapshot for PH-353 import submission; it is not an amount authorization and must be server-recomputed, with stale/blocked rejection. No persistence table is added by this contract; PH-353 owns storing the digest with its submission.
No code, migration, table, route, contract schema, gate or acceptance-command change; the capability remains not implemented (PH-181/PH-185 follow-up).
